channel.title: The Western Producer - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Western Producer (producer.com)

item.title: Monitoring network casts light on below-ground farm water reserves
item.description: National soil moisture sensor network gives real-time data for Manitoba farmers fighting more frequent drought or flood.

item.title: India, Canada aim for trade pact by year-end, propose pulse protein ‘centre of excellence’
item.description: India and Canada will aim to conclude a free trade pact by the end of this year, Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Monday during his first visit to New Delhi.

item.title: China slashes anti-dumping tariff on Canadian canola in final ruling
item.description: China on Saturday sharply reduced its tariff rate on Canadian canola seed in the final ruling of a 17-month anti-dumping investigation, following a thaw in relations between Beijing and Ottawa.

item.title: Applications open for 2026 Advance Payments Program: Canadian Canola Growers
item.description: Farmers can now submit applications for a 2026 cash advance through the Canadian Canola Growers Association, which administers the federal Advance Payments Program.

item.title: Some fertilizer prices rise as Iran conflict escalates
item.description: Some fertilizer prices surged following the impact of the escalating Middle East conflict on supplies moving through the Strait of Hormuz, analysts told Reuters on Monday.

item.title: Possible delays, detours expected from oversize load in Regina area
item.description: Highways and grid roads in the Regina area will be affected by a large building move this week and drivers are encouraged to seek alternate routes.

item.title: Sun, insolation and the solar constant
item.description: When climatologists and meteorologists talk about incoming energy from the sun, we use the term insolation.

item.title: Iran conflict drives up urea prices
item.description: The war in Iran is already driving up urea prices in North American and will likely impact phosphate as well, say analysts.

item.title: U.S. to seek more foreign tariff cuts, CUSMA improvements in 2026
item.description: The U.S. Trade Representative’s office said on Monday it will seek further reductions in foreign tariffs and non-tariff barriers this year, enforce its “reciprocal” trade deals and consider launching new unfair trade practices investigations.
